title: Pollution and Health Consequences of Distortionary Fertilizer Subsidies
HarvestStat: a global effort towards open and standardized sub-national agricultural data
abstract: Agricultural production statistics underpin diverse research efforts and development activities. Yet despite their critical importance, efforts to collate, update, and harmonize detailed sub-national agricultural production statistics are frequently redundant and incomplete due to the substantial time, effort, and resources required. The persisting lack of coordination and standards in the food systems data community wastes valuable resources and hinders advances in action-oriented food systems knowledge. Here we introduce the HarvestStat sub-national data consortium as an open-source, collaborative, and transparent model to overcome these challenges. HarvestStat is collaboratively producing publicly available databases and datasets for the food systems community and the broader environmental and sustainability sciences by moving beyond closed and disjointed data-gathering efforts. We are guided by core principles of complete data openness—prioritizing high standards of quality assurance; active inclusion—emphasizing involvement from local experts; and collaboration—fostering engagement across communities of data producers and users. We extend an open global call to action, inviting organizations and individuals to engage in advancing this critical agenda.
abstract_zh: 农业生产统计数据是各类研究与发展活动的基础。然而，尽管其至关重要，但由于收集、更新和统一详细的次国家级农业生产统计需要大量的时间、精力和资源，相关工作往往重复且不完整。粮食系统数据界长期缺乏协调与标准，浪费了宝贵的资源，也阻碍了以行动为导向的粮食系统知识的进步。在此，我们推出HarvestStat次国家级数据联盟，作为一种开放源代码、协作且透明的模式，以应对这些挑战。HarvestStat正在协作建设可供公众获取的数据库和数据集，服务于粮食系统研究界以及更广泛的环境与可持续性科学领域，从而超越封闭且分散的数据收集努力。我们以以下核心原则为指导：完全的数据开放——优先保证高标准的质量保证；积极纳入——强调本地专家的参与；以及协作——促进数据生产者与使用者社群之间的交流。我们向所有组织和个人发出开放的全球行动倡议，邀请其共同推进这一关键议程。

title: Impacts of Climate Change on Global Agriculture Accounting for Adaptation
abstract: Climate change threatens global food systems1, but the extent to which adaptation will reduce losses remains unknown and controversial2. Even within the well-studied context of US agriculture, some analyses argue that adaptation will be widespread and climate damages small3,4, whereas others conclude that adaptation will be limited and losses severe5,6. Scenario-based analyses indicate that adaptation should have notable consequences on global agricultural productivity7–9, but there has been no systematic study of how extensively real-world producers actually adapt at the global scale. Here we empirically estimate the impact of global producer adaptations using longitudinal data on six staple crops spanning 12,658 regions, capturing two-thirds of global crop calories. We estimate that global production declines 5.5 × 1014 kcal annually per 1 °C global mean surface temperature (GMST) rise (120 kcal per person per day or 4.4% of recommended consumption per 1 °C; P < 0.001). We project that adaptation and income growth alleviate 23% of global losses in 2050 and 34% at the end of the century (6% and 12%, respectively; moderate-emissions scenario), but substantial residual losses remain for all staples except rice. In contrast to analyses of other outcomes that project the greatest damages to the global poor10,11, we find that global impacts are dominated by losses to modern-day breadbaskets with favourable climates and limited present adaptation, although losses in low-income regions losses are also substantial. These results indicate a scale of innovation, cropland expansion or further adaptation that might be necessary to ensure food security in a changing climate. Analysis of data on six stable crops, capturing two-thirds of global crop calories, allows estimation of agricultural impacts and the potential of global producer adaptations to reduce output losses owing to climate change.
abstract_zh: 气候变化威胁着全球粮食系统[1]，但适应措施能在多大程度上减少损失，目前仍不清楚且存在争议[2]。即使在研究充分的美国农业背景下，一些分析认为适应将广泛发生，气候损害较小[3,4]，而另一些分析则认为适应将十分有限，损失严重[5,6]。基于情景的分析表明，适应应当对全球农业生产力产生显著影响[7–9]，但目前尚无系统研究考察现实中的生产者在全球范围内究竟在多大程度上进行了适应。在此，我们利用覆盖12,658个地区的六种主要粮食作物的纵向数据，对全球生产者适应的影响进行了实证估计，这些作物占全球作物热量的三分之二。我们估计，全球平均地表温度（GMST）每上升1°C，全球产量每年下降5.5×10^14千卡（相当于每人每天120千卡，或推荐摄入量的4.4%，P < 0.001）。我们预测，到2050年，适应与收入增长将挽回全球损失的23%，到本世纪末将挽回34%（在中等排放情景下，分别为6%和12%）；但除水稻外，所有主粮仍存在大量剩余损失。与其他结果的分析（这些分析预测全球贫困人口将遭受最大损害）[10,11]不同，我们发现全球影响主要由当今气候条件良好、目前适应程度有限的主要粮仓地区的损失所主导，尽管低收入地区的损失也相当可观。这些结果表明，为确保气候变化下的粮食安全，可能需要相应规模的创新、耕地扩张或进一步的适应措施。对覆盖全球作物热量三分之二的六种稳定作物的数据进行分析，使我们能够估计农业影响，以及全球生产者适应减少气候变化所致产出损失的潜力。

title: Innovation and lobbying in response to regulatory uncertainty
Valuing the global mortality consequences of climate change accounting for adaptation costs and benefits
abstract: Using 40 countries’ subnational data, we estimate age-specific mortality-temperature relationships and extrapolate them to countries without data today and into a future with climate change. We uncover a U-shaped relationship where extre6me cold and hot temperatures increase mortality rates, especially for the elderly. Critically, this relationship is flattened by higher incomes and adaptation to local climate. Using a revealed-preference approach to recover unobserved adaptation costs, we estimate that the mean global increase in mortality risk due to climate change, accounting for adaptation benefits and costs, is valued at roughly 3.2% of global GDP in 2100 under a high-emissions scenario. Notably, today’s cold locations are projected to benefit, while today’s poor and hot locations have large projected damages. Finally, our central estimates indicate that the release of an additional ton of CO2 today will cause mortality-related damages of $36.6 under a high-emissions scenario, with an interquartile range accounting for both econometric and climate uncertainty of [−$7.8, $73.0]. These empirically grounded estimates exceed the previous literature’s estimates by an order of magnitude.
abstract_zh: 利用40个国家的次国家级数据，我们估计了分年龄组的死亡率与温度之间的关系，并将其外推至当前缺乏数据的国家以及气候变化背景下的未来情景。我们发现了一种U形关系：极端的低温和高温会提高死亡率，对老年人尤为明显。关键在于，这一关系会因收入水平提高和当地气候适应而趋于平缓。我们采用显示性偏好方法（revealed-preference approach）来推算不可观测的适应成本，估计在高排放情景下，考虑适应收益与适应成本之后，气候变化导致的全球平均死亡风险增加在2100年约相当于全球GDP的3.2%。值得注意的是，当前较为寒冷的地区预计将从中受益，而当前贫穷且炎热的地区预计将遭受巨大损失。最后，我们的中心估计表明，在高排放情景下，当前每排放一吨CO2将造成36.6美元的死亡率相关损害，若同时考虑计量经济学不确定性与气候不确定性，其四分位距为[−7.8美元，73.0美元]。这些基于经验证据的估计，比以往文献的估计高出一个数量级。

title: Labor Disutility in a Warmer World: The impact of climate change on the global workforce
abstract: This paper develops the first globally comprehensive and empirically grounded estimates of worker disutility due to future temperature increases caused by climate change. Harmonizing daily worker-level data from seven countries representing nearly a third of the world's population, we first evaluate the causal effect of daily temperature on labor supply, recovering an inverted U-shaped relationship where extreme cold and hot temperatures lead to labor supply losses for workers in weather-exposed industries. We then develop the first micro-founded, global estimates for how future climate change will impact workers, accounting for expected shifts in the global workforce towards less weather-exposed industries. Interpreting labor supply impacts of climate change through a simple theoretical framework, we monetize the implied disutility to workers of a warmer climate, a welfare cost not captured in any existing estimates. Under a high emissions scenario, we estimate the increase in labor disutility is valued at roughly 1.8% of global GDP in 2099, with damages being especially large in today’s poor and/or hot locations while cold locations benefit. Finally, we estimate that the release of an additional ton of CO2 today will cause expected labor disutility damages of $17.0 under a high emissions scenario and $10.8 under a moderate scenario, using a 2% discount rate that is justified by US Treasury rates over the last two decades. Accounting for uncertainty in these marginal damages when individuals are risk averse increases their value by 31% (high emissions scenario) and 62% (moderate scenario) under a standard parameterization of the utility function.
abstract_zh: 本文首次对未来气温升高（由气候变化引起）给劳动者带来的负效用进行了全球范围内的全面且基于经验证据的估计。我们协调了来自七个国家的逐日劳动者层面数据，这些国家的人口约占世界总人口的三分之一。我们首先评估了日气温对劳动供给的因果效应，得到一种倒U形关系：在受天气影响较大的行业中，极端的低温和高温都会导致劳动者的劳动供给减少。随后，我们首次基于微观基础建立了全球范围内的估计，考察未来气候变化将如何影响劳动者，并考虑全球劳动力向受天气影响较小的行业转移的预期变化。我们通过一个简单的理论框架来解释气候变化对劳动供给的影响，并将由此隐含的、更温暖气候给劳动者带来的负效用货币化，这是现有估计均未涵盖的福利成本。在高排放情景下，我们估计2099年劳动负效用的增加相当于全球GDP的约1.8%，其中损失在当前贫穷和/或炎热的地区尤为严重，而寒冷地区则从中受益。最后，我们估计，在高排放情景下，当前每排放一吨CO2将造成17.0美元的预期劳动负效用损失，在中等排放情景下为10.8美元，贴现率取2%，该贴现率由过去二十年美国国债收益率予以支持。若风险厌恶型个体的不确定性被纳入考虑，并采用效用函数的标准参数化设定，则在高排放情景下其价值将提高31%，在中等排放情景下提高62%。

title: Estimating a social cost of carbon for global energy consumption
abstract: Estimates of global economic damage caused by carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions can inform climate policy. The social cost of carbon (SCC) quantifies these damages by characterizing how additional CO2 emissions today impact future economic outcomes through altering the climate. Previous estimates suggest that large, warming-driven increases in energy expenditures could dominate the SCC, but they rely on models that are spatially coarse and not tightly linked to data. Here we show that the release of 1t CO2 today is projected to reduce total future energy expenditures, with most estimates valued between -$3 and -$1, depending on discount rates. Our results are based on a new architecture that integrates global data, econometrics, and climate science to estimate local dam- ages worldwide. Notably, we project that emerging economies in the tropics will dramatically increase electricity consumption due to warming, requiring critical infrastructure planning. However, heating reductions in colder countries offset this increase globally. We estimate that 2099 global electricity consumption rises ∼ 4.5 EJ/yr (7% current global consumption) while direct consumption of other fuels declines ∼ 11.3 EJ/yr (7% current consumption) per +1◦C increase in global mean temperature. Our finding of net savings contradicts previous research, because global data indicate that many populations will remain too poor for most of the 21st century to substantially increase energy consumption in response to warming. Importantly, damage estimates would differ if poorer populations were given greater weight.
abstract_zh: 对二氧化碳（CO2）排放造成的全球经济损害进行估计，可以为气候政策提供依据。碳的社会成本（SCC）刻画了当前额外的二氧化碳排放如何通过改变气候而影响未来的经济结果，从而量化这些损害。以往的估计表明，由变暖驱动的能源支出大幅增加可能主导碳的社会成本，但这些估计依赖于空间粗糙且与数据联系不紧密的模型。在此我们表明，当前排放1吨二氧化碳预计将减少未来的总能源支出，根据不同的贴现率，大多数估计值介于负3美元至负1美元之间。我们的结果基于一种新的架构，该架构整合了全球数据、计量经济学和气候科学，以估计全球各地的局部损害。值得注意的是，我们预测热带新兴经济体的电力消耗将因变暖而大幅增加，这需要关键的基础设施规划。然而，寒冷国家供暖需求的减少在全球范围内抵消了这一增长。我们估计，全球平均气温每上升1°C，到2099年全球电力消费将增加约4.5艾焦/年（相当于当前全球消费的7%），而其他燃料的直接消费将减少约11.3艾焦/年（相当于当前消费的7%）。我们关于净节约的发现与以往研究相矛盾，原因在于全球数据表明，许多人口在二十一世纪大部分时间里仍将过于贫穷，无法因变暖而大幅增加能源消费。重要的是，如果赋予较贫穷人口更大的权重，损害估计将会有所不同。

title: The effect of large-scale anti-contagion policies on the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic
